unit: writer and timing/sound (nonhuman account, cue sheet, stems)

conventions.frames: 0-based film frames at 24 fps; frame f covers [f/24, (f+1)/24) s
conventions.write_start_frame: first ink of the first letter
conventions.cps: characters incl. spaces and punctuation * 24 / (write_end - write_start); target 11-14
conventions.one_hand: a single pen writes serially; no two write-ons overlap (checked)
conventions.anchors: write_start anchors: ink begins within +/-1 frame of the image event; S6 'Krach !' anchors on write completion (f605); the strike anchors on f528

witness.perceptual_limits: only what is in the panel or its own field; no names, dates, numbers, physics terms; cannot read
witness.voice: first person, one hand, one paper stock

struck_word.placement: s'arrêter is written above the struck word

changes_from_plan_lines: S1b 'Le papier plie quand il veut. Le mien, quand je veux.' (52 chars) -> 'La mienne obéit.' (16): the original needs 3.7 s at 14 cps and would run through the 'pof' at f154. The comparison with the bird's own wing is kept.
S2 'Ensuite, un moulin à élastique.' -> 'Puis un moulin à élastique.' so it ends before the release at f254.

S2b 'Il le lâche, et le moulin monte tout seul. Lui reste en bas. C'est sage : il faut bien quelqu'un pour regarder.' (110 chars, about 8 s) -> 'Lui reste en bas. C'est sage.' (fits the release-to-snap window f254-f312).

S3 moved from the page turn (16.6 s) to f346-f389, beside sheet 1's third panel: after the turn there is no room to write S3, S4 and 'monter' by f527 at 14 cps or less. DEPENDENCY: s1p3 must show the glider at rest so the bird can see 'les grandes ailes'.
S4 'Il court face au vent. Bien.' -> 'Face au vent. Bien.' (the image already shows the running).
S5b 'Moi aussi, quand je veux me poser.' (34 chars, 2.4 s) -> 'Moi aussi, pour me poser.' (25): it must finish by f592 so 'Krach !' can complete at f605 with one hand.
S6 'Donc il se pose.' dropped before the impact: no room between S5b and 'Krach !'. Its inference ('he is landing') is carried by S5b ('pour me poser') and S6b/S6c.
S6b/S6c 'Un peu vite. Mais au bon endroit.' split in two slips so 'au bon endroit' is anchored on the magpie's own landing beside the wreck (f638).

cues.image_event: push-in completes on panel 1: the man on the wall with a ribbed paper wing strapped to his arm
cues.text: Il s'est fait une aile en papier.
cues.gloss_en_graphite: He made himself a wing out of paper.
cues.hand: pen.hand (Hershey-derived, per-word slant/size/baseline drift, felt nib), warm ink (65,53,41) on torn cream slip, brass pin
cues.contrast: The image shows a paper shape tied to an arm. The slip adds the bird's surprise that a wing can be made at all ('s'est fait'): a wing is something it grows.

witness_gate.perception: bird perched on the gatepost in panel 1, head toward him

cues.image_event: third flap: the paper wing tip folds back on itself
cues.gloss_en_graphite: Mine does what I tell it.
cues.hand: pen.hand (Hershey-derived, per-word slant/size/baseline drift, felt nib), warm ink (65,53,41) on torn cream slip, brass pin
cues.contrast: The image shows the paper tip folding by itself. The slip compares it with the bird's own wing, which folds only when the bird wants: the failure is disobedience, not weakness.

witness_gate.perception: bird's head at the 3rd held angle (f100), toward the wing

cues.image_event: he sits down on the flowerbed
cues.hand: pen.hand (Hershey-derived, per-word slant/size/baseline drift, felt nib), warm ink (65,53,41) on torn cream slip, brass pin
cues.contrast: Sound word: the bird hears the sit as soft and harmless (a 'pof', not a fall). Carried with S1b.

witness_gate.perception: bird's head at 5th held angle (f150), on him

cues.image_event: he winds the two-rotor machine in steps (12 turns, tally in graphite)
cues.hand: pen.hand (Hershey-derived, per-word slant/size/baseline drift, felt nib), warm ink (65,53,41) on torn cream slip, brass pin
fx: rubber creak per winding step f192-f250 (30 steps on 2s)
cues.contrast: The image shows a winding machine. The slip names it as the bird sees it, a 'moulin', a thing that turns where it is, not a flier.

witness_gate.perception: bird perched in panel 2 at left

cues.image_event: release: the rotor rises out of his hands; he stays on the ground
cues.text: Lui reste en bas. C'est sage.
cues.hand: pen.hand (Hershey-derived, per-word slant/size/baseline drift, felt nib), warm ink (65,53,41) on torn cream slip, brass pin
cues.contrast: The image shows only the machine rising and the man staying. The slip approves: staying down to watch first is what the bird calls wise.

witness_gate.perception: bird looks up (head 35 deg) from f254

cues.image_event: the rubber band snaps (pen squiggle whips)
cues.hand: pen.hand (Hershey-derived, per-word slant/size/baseline drift, felt nib), warm ink (65,53,41) on torn cream slip, brass pin
fx: small thump f331 (machine drops on turf)
cues.contrast: Sound word only: the bird hears the snap. Carried with S2b (no added claim).

witness_gate.perception: bird head up 50 deg toward the rotor

cues.image_event: REQUIRES sheet-1 panel 3 to show the glider at rest (still key pose), visible in the pull-out f384-f396
cues.hand: pen.hand (Hershey-derived, per-word slant/size/baseline drift, felt nib), warm ink (65,53,41) on torn cream slip, brass pin
cues.contrast: The image shows a large frame of cloth and spars. 'grandes ailes' measures it the bird's way, by wings, and 'Enfin' says that, to a bird, this at last looks like the real thing.

witness_gate.perception: DEPENDENCY: passes only if s1p3 holds the resting glider (board artist); fallback: drop S3, nothing else moves

cues.image_event: the run starts down the pen hill, right to left
cues.hand: pen.hand (Hershey-derived, per-word slant/size/baseline drift, felt nib), warm ink (65,53,41) on torn cream slip, brass pin
cues.contrast: The image shows a man running downhill. The slip adds the bird's own take-off rule (into the wind) and approves it.

witness_gate.perception: bird on the fence post in panel s2p1

cues.image_event: lift-off f490; nose starts to come up after f504
cues.text: Il lève le nez pour monter
cues.gloss_en_graphite: He lifts his nose to ~~climb~~ stop.
cues.hand: pen.hand (Hershey-derived, per-word slant/size/baseline drift, felt nib), warm ink (65,53,41) on torn cream slip, brass pin
cues.contrast: Written as the man's intention ('to climb'), so the bird can correct it at the strike.

witness_gate.perception: bird on the post in panel s2p2, watching the lift-off

cues.image_event: nose crosses 15 deg above the horizon, forward advance dying (exposure: nose_15deg_frame 528)
cues.hand: pen.hand (Hershey-derived, per-word slant/size/baseline drift, felt nib), warm ink (65,53,41) on torn cream slip, brass pin
cues.contrast: The strike is the bird changing its mind on the page: what looked like climbing is, to a flier, the start of stopping.

witness_gate.perception: bird in panel 2 (on post, takes off ~f538)

cues.image_event: pitch reaches 35 deg, x-advance zero at f540; hang f540-f554 with legs still swinging
cues.hand: pen.hand (Hershey-derived, per-word slant/size/baseline drift, felt nib), warm ink (65,53,41) on torn cream slip, brass pin
cues.contrast: The image shows nose up and forward motion ceasing. The slip gives the bird's reading: a raised nose is how you stop. It reads braking, not failure.

cues.image_event: the magpie flies level past him and flares nose-up at f560 (the same gesture, done right)
cues.hand: pen.hand (Hershey-derived, per-word slant/size/baseline drift, felt nib), warm ink (65,53,41) on torn cream slip, brass pin
fx: paste flap SUPPRESSED (paste f547 falls in the declared silence)
cues.contrast: The image shows two nose-up shapes. The slip says they are the same act and that its purpose is landing: the man is doing what birds do to come down.

witness_gate.perception: the bird is the subject; flying through panel 2

cues.image_event: impact: glider shadow and glider touch the turf
cues.hand: pen.hand (Hershey-derived, per-word slant/size/baseline drift, felt nib), warm ink (65,53,41) on torn cream slip, brass pin
cues.contrast: Sound word: on its own it paraphrases the image (gate 4 fails alone). It is carried by S6b/S6c, which turn the crash into a landing.

witness_gate.perception: bird perched at the panel 2/3 edge after its landing f568-f580; NEEDS head turned to the wreck at f580-f605 (or bird visible at the edge of panel 3)

cues.image_event: the wreck is held; legs whip and settle by f636
cues.hand: pen.hand (Hershey-derived, per-word slant/size/baseline drift, felt nib), warm ink (65,53,41) on torn cream slip, brass pin
cues.contrast: The image shows a wreck. The slip grades it as a landing that was a bit fast, which is how a bird judges any landing.

cues.image_event: the magpie lands beside the wreck with a clean flare (two-hop settle, one peck)
cues.hand: pen.hand (Hershey-derived, per-word slant/size/baseline drift, felt nib), warm ink (65,53,41) on torn cream slip, brass pin
cues.contrast: The image shows the bird landing next to the wreck. The slip says the place was right: the man came down where a bird would choose to.

fx: page turn swoosh, flip edge peak f408 (exposure: turn f396-f418)
sound_only_cues.note: The task text puts the page turn at 16 s (f384). The exposure sheet has the pull-out f384-f394 and the turn f396-f418, so the sound follows the exposure.

The magpie whoosh (task: f548-f560) is moved to start at f554 (peak f557) so the declared silence holds. The bird is seen approaching in silence and heard only as it passes. S5b's paste flap (f547) is suppressed for the same reason.

fx: air fades out over the last 2.5 s
sound_only_cues.note: S6c's write-on ends at f674, 14 frames into BB-10's pull-out; the full-sheet hold from about f684 shows every slip complete.

S5b paste f547 / write f549-f592 (board.py has f552, cps 12.5, with the longer text: replace it with 'Moi aussi, pour me poser.').

evidence.title: File:Pica pica.ogg
evidence.author: Oona Räisänen (Mysid)
evidence.license: Public domain (Commons extmetadata LicenseShortName 'Public domain', read 2026-11-16)
evidence.what_it_shows: Sound, 26.5 s: a Eurasian magpie (Pica pica) in a backyard in southern Finland, two kinds of call (the rattling chatter and single 'chack' calls); a house sparrow faint in the background. Spectrogram checked: 6 chatter bursts at about 30 dB above the floor.

absences: File:Pica pica - Eurasian Magpie XC537413.mp3 (CC BY-SA 4.0, Benoît Van Hecke, France 2020; the researcher's pick): metadata read, but upload.wikimedia.org answered HTTP 429 with retry-after 600 s repeatedly; not downloaded. The PD recording above replaced it, so no CC BY-SA attribution is needed for sound.
Other Commons magpie calls seen in search (XC432921, XC475651, XC478076, XC551758, all CC BY-SA 4.0; W1CDR0001537 BD28, CC BY-SA 4.0): not needed; not downloaded.

Moving Image Archive cache: no magpie or corvid call; the refuge films are narrated and the bird clips are scored. Speech-free outdoor air exists only in 1.6-2.4 s spans (the researcher scanned every clip with sound).
No foraged paper, rubber, pin or impact recordings under an allowed licence were looked for beyond the cache. All FX are handmade synthesis, which the brief allows and the plan specifies.

numpy: a sheet swoosh peaking at the flip edge f408, crinkled edge, then the settle flap at f418
numpy: band noise with sparse crackle impulses
numpy: stick-slip pulse train, pitch and level rising with tension over 30 steps on 2s

numpy: a bright tick + 3.15/4.73 kHz ring decaying in 60 ms

handmade.made: numpy: band noise in a Hann window, amplitude-beaten at 12 beats/s (wings on 2s)
